Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:51: Therefore whoever is a communal leader, judge, or charity collector must not be a flatterer — for if he flatters someone and does not rebuke him to do good and turn from evil, then the whole community will become corrupted through him, each one saying, "the leader flatters so-and-so, why should he rebuke me, since he flatters him?" — and they will not accept his rebukes. Likewise, a judge who flatters one of the litigants — then the words of the other party will be stifled and he will not know how to argue properly, and the judgment will not come out true. Likewise, flattering charity collectors will give charity to one who flatters them, or whom they flatter, and give to him even though he is unworthy. Therefore the righteous person must distance himself greatly from flattery — neither flattering others nor accepting flattery from others. And he must be very careful, when doing good deeds, not to intend thereby to flatter others, but to do them for the sake of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:52: The worst of all flattery is one who flatters his fellow in order to cause him to sin — such as one who has a dispute with people and the law is not on his side, and he flatters people to help him and support his error. Or one who pursues transgressions, such as licentiousness and other transgressions, and flatters his fellow so that he do the same as him. Jeroboam son of Nebat merited the kingship because he did not flatter King Solomon but rebuked him regarding the matter of the Millo (Sanhedrin 101b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:53: Whoever wishes to be saved from flattery should be careful to distance himself from honor, for one who does not care about being honored will not need flattery, and he must also be careful of others, since most flatterers flatter a person whom they think will benefit them. Therefore whoever distances himself from these two things — benefit and honor — is saved from many transgressions, for many people do good deeds in order to receive honor from people, and this matter corrupts all of a person's service — for how many people pray with a pleasant voice, and think in their heart during prayer, "How pleasant is my voice, and how many people enjoy listening to me!" This is the way of the evil inclination, acting so as to trap a person in its net, so that his deeds not be for the sake of Heaven. Likewise regarding benefit: one who benefits from his fellow, even if he sees him transgressing all the sins in the world, will not dare to rebuke him, fearing he will no longer benefit from him. This matter is the downfall of the sages of the generation, for they pursue benefit from the people, and therefore flatter them so that they hold onto them firmly — and it is not enough that they do not rebuke them for their matters, but through flattering them, they themselves take up their deeds and are drawn after them — so far. Rabbeinu Moshe [Maimonides] wrote this in Hilchot De'ot.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:54: In explaining the class of liars — that is, the class of falsifiers — one who lies and deceives is hated and abominable before the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, "there are six things the Lord hates..." (Proverbs 6:16) — haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood, one who breathes forth lies, one who sows discord, a heart that devises wicked thoughts, feet that hasten [to run to evil]. Of these seven things, three of them concern the matter of falsehood — a lying tongue, one who breathes forth lies, a false witness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:55: Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said that these seven evil traits are all hung upon falsehood, from which they all descend. How so? "Haughty eyes" — the essence of arrogance is falsehood, because he says he is wise when he is a fool, mighty when he is weak, a prince when he is lowly, and he glorifies himself before people in these traits of falsehood, as Absalom said, "and let anyone who has a suit or cause come to me, and I would do him justice" (II Samuel 15:4), stealing people's minds through falsehood.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:56: "A lying tongue" — the falsehood itself. "Hands that shed innocent blood" — from Joab, who sent a false message in David's name and brought back Abner and killed him, as it is said, "and he sent messengers after Abner..." (II Samuel 3:26). "One who breathes forth lies, a false witness" — behold, the very substances of falsehood. "And one who sows discord between brothers" — as it is said, "Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongues..." (Psalms 55:10), and adjacent to it, "mischief and trouble are within her; wickedness is within her; deceit and guile depart not from her streets" (Psalms 55:11-12).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:57: Come and see how much they lied and were punished. Gehazi lied and was stricken with tzara'at, he and his descendants, as it is said, "and Elisha said to him, From where, Gehazi? And he said, Your servant did not go anywhere. And he said to him, My heart did not go..." (II Kings 5:25-26), "and the tzara'at of Naaman shall cling to you and to your descendants forever; and he went out from before him leprous as snow." Amnon lied and was killed, as it is said, "let Tamar my sister come and make a couple of cakes before my eyes..." (II Samuel 13:5) — "and lie with her," and Absalom killed him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:58: Whoever changes his speech is as though he worshiped idols, as it is said, "perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver" (m'ta'te'a) (Genesis 27:12), and it is written regarding idolatry, "they are vanity, a work of deceptions (ta'tu'im)" (Jeremiah 51:18) (Sanhedrin 92b). Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab explains in the book Menorat HaMa'or (letter 37) regarding this matter, why he should be like an idol worshiper: the intent is that because he deceives his fellow with a false matter, according to this, one who deceives his fellow in any manner whatsoever should also be considered thus, because he resembles idolatry, which likewise deceives people by claiming to have power.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:59: Rabbi Elazar said, the Holy One, blessed be He, created everything except falsehood, which He did not create — rather, people fabricate it from their own minds (Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, ch. 3). We learn in the Midrash that the spirit of Naboth the Jezreelite did not merit the supernal abode except because Ahab killed him for innocent blood, and it was absent because it had thought to speak falsehoods, as it is said, "who shall entice Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth..." (I Kings 22:20), "and the spirit came forth and said, I will entice him..." and "the Lord said, Go forth" — what is "the spirit"? This is the spirit of Naboth. What is "go forth"? Go forth from My presence, because "one who speaks falsehoods shall not be established before my eyes" (Psalms 101:7).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:60: The sage said, a person who lies is considered like dead, for people do not pay attention to his words because it is his habit to lie — his life and death are equal. And they say, of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 89b), this is the punishment of the liar — that even when he speaks the truth, they do not listen to him. And when Jeremiah rebuked Israel, he rebuked them only regarding falsehood, as it is said, "they have taught their tongue to speak lies" (Jeremiah 9:4) — falsehood became a habit for them, and they could not turn away from it, and they wearied themselves trying to turn from the path of falsehood to the path of truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:61: Rav Huna said, we find that Israel was exiled from their land only because they transgressed this verse, "keep far from a false matter" (Exodus 23:7); and in the Book of Lamentations it is alluded to in three places: in the acrostic "Eichah ya'ib" ("How He has clouded [in His anger]"), Peh precedes Ayin, meaning they spoke with their mouths what they had not seen with their eyes, as it is written, "they have opened their mouth wide against you" (Lamentations 2:16), and afterward, "the Lord has done what He devised" (2:17). And in the acrostic "Ani ha'gever" ("I am the man"), "they have opened their mouth against us" (3:46), and afterward, "my eye runs down" (3:49). And in the acrostic "Eichah yu'am zahav" ("How the gold has become dim"), "the presence of the Lord has divided them" (4:16), and afterward, "our eyes still fail" (4:17).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:62: We learn in the chapter HaBa Al Yevimto (Yevamot 63a): Rav Huna's wife used to trouble him — when he told her to make him lentils, she made him beans; when he wanted beans, she made him lentils. When his son Chiya grew up, he would reverse [the message] to her. [Rav Huna] said to him, "Your mother has improved!" He said to him, "It is I who reversed it." He said to him, "This is what people say: 'from you comes the practice that you taught yourself' [i.e., you learned deception from me] — but you must not do this," as it is said, "they have taught their tongue to speak lies" — therefore let him teach his tongue to speak truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:63: Rabbeinu Yonah writes in Sha'arei Teshuvah (Gate 3, item 181) that this is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, meant by saying, "he who breathes forth lies is a false witness" (Proverbs 6:19) — meaning, one who is accustomed to speaking falsehood even regarding worldly matters, all the more so will he lie and testify falsely against his fellow, because of his nature and the habit of his tongue.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:64: Rabbeinu Yonah wrote (Gate 3, item 178) that the class of liars divides into nine parts, and the author of Menorat HaMa'or, Rabbi Yisrael, peace be upon him, condensed his wording and established it in seven, in these words:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:65: The first part: a man of lies — not only does he lie, but through his lies he destroys, robs, and extorts, like one who denies [a debt to] his fellow, or withholds a hired worker's wage, transgressing the commandments "you shall not deny falsely" and "you shall not lie" (Leviticus 19:11) and "it shall not remain [overnight with you]" (Leviticus 19:13); and likewise one who testifies falsely against his fellow, as it is said, "you shall not testify falsely against your neighbor" (Exodus 20:13). From this part [comes] the master of deceptions and frauds in trade and partnerships, and it is written, "you shall not defraud" (Leviticus 25:17); and the liar is called "Belial" and "a man of iniquity," as it is said, "a base person, a man of iniquity..." (Proverbs 6:12).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:66: Second: one who lies and deceives his fellow, and there is no immediate harm from this lie, but he intends to create a cause to harm him later — such as one who deceives his fellow so that he trusts and relies on him and does not guard himself, in order to bring loss upon him — in the manner of what is said, "with his mouth one speaks peace to his neighbor..." (Jeremiah 9:7), and it is written after it, "shall I not visit them for these things?" This one is punished for three things: the falsehood, the harm, and the loss.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:67: Third: one who comes with cunning to divert to himself the good fortune of his fellow — not to rob or extort his fellow, but he sets his eyes on the good fortune destined to come to his fellow and, through his lies, maneuvers until he takes it for himself. How so? For example, he sees his fellow buying merchandise cheaply, and goes to the seller and says to him, "I will give you more money for this merchandise, and don't worry about so-and-so, for we are partners." Or he maneuvers so that his fellow gives him gifts because of his lies — such as saying to him, "I wish to buy such-and-such land, which you wish to buy," and the other gives him money so that he withdraws from the land and does not take it. Or he says to him, "I was a good advocate for you with the king or with the officer," and anything similar to this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:68: Fourth: one who tells a story he has heard and changes part of it, without any benefit to himself or loss to his fellow; even though he does not cause loss to others, his punishment is very great, because he brazenly lies from his own evil nature. But they permitted changing in matters involving a mitzvah, or for the sake of bringing peace, for it was taught (see Ketubot 17a) that they praise the bride before the groom and say "a beautiful and graceful bride," even if she is not beautiful. And we learn in Bereshit Rabbah (100:8), it is permitted to alter [the truth] for the sake of peace, as it is said, "your father commanded..." (Genesis 50:16), whereas we do not find that Jacob commanded any such thing — rather they said it in his name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:69: Fifth: one who tells his fellow that he will do well by him and give him gifts, without any intent in his heart to give him anything — this too is a great evil, and concerning it is said, "guard your tongue from evil" (Psalms 34:14). And one who boasts of a false gift, to what may this be compared? To many clouds and winds, and it appears that rain has come, but it does not fall, as it is said, "clouds and wind without rain" (Proverbs 25:14).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:70: Sixth: one who boasts that he did good for his fellow when he did not, and it is not enough for him that he lies, but he also steals people's minds — for it was taught (see Chullin 94a) that it is forbidden to steal people's minds, even the mind of a gentile; one may not sell a gentile the meat of an unslaughtered or fallen animal in place of properly slaughtered meat, nor a shoe made from the hide of a fallen animal in place of the hide of a slaughtered one; and a person should not show his fellow that he is opening a barrel for his sake when he really wishes to open it for a shopkeeper; and he should not multiply invitations to his fellow knowing he will not accept. Such matters and the like are forbidden for several reasons: because he lies, and because he steals people's minds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:71: Seventh: one who boasts of virtues he does not have — such as saying he is a prince and of distinguished lineage, and that his ancestors were great men of their generation; not only is he arrogant and exalting himself, but he is also lying. Concerning this King Solomon, peace be upon him, said, "excessive speech is not fitting for a base person" (Proverbs 17:7) — meaning, it is not fitting for one who is base and from a lowly family to say he is a prince and great; "how much less for a noble to speak falsehood" — meaning, even if he is a prince and noble in his deeds, he should not lie with his lips and boast that he gives gifts to people when he has not given — for even if he did give, it is disgraceful for a person to boast of his own gifts, all the more so for a noble. And if there are people who honor him with degrees of honor, such as saying of him that he is a sage, he should say, "I am not a sage." Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yerushalmi Makkot 3:6) that whoever is honored with degrees of honor fitting for one who knows two tractates, when he knows only one, must say, "I know only one alone" — how much more is it forbidden to boast of what one does not have — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:72: Regarding the greatness of one who speaks truth and the punishment of one who speaks falsehood, they elaborate at length in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 63, 94b), in these words: what is "the Lord is near to all who call upon Him" (Psalms 145:18)? Whoever calls upon Him falsely is far from Him. "Emet" (truth) — Aleph at the beginning of the alphabet, Mem in the middle, Tav at the end; its tenth part is Yod-Kei Vav-Kei, "emet" whose tenth part is 441, behold the mystery of forty-five (45). At the time Israel lie regarding the Torah of truth, it is said of it, "and it cast truth to the ground" (Daniel 8:12) — what is "to the ground"? This is the Shechinah. And in exile, "and truth is lacking" (Isaiah 59:15), and falsehood rules in the world — and who is falsehood? This is Samael. At the time truth rules, falsehood departs from the world. "Emet" is at the end of words, and these are "bara Elohim la'asot," "bara Elohim et" — through it He created the world, and by it it is called and the whole world stands, and all the nations of the world. But with falsehood, "and it cast truth to the ground," and falsehood rules, as it were, in its own place, which is Jerusalem — and this causes the Temple to be destroyed and return to formlessness and void, for so they established: the First Temple was destroyed and "the earth was formless and void" (Genesis 1:2); the Second Temple was destroyed and "darkness was upon the face of the deep" (ibid.) — for truth surrounds above and below, and at the time falsehood is done, the structure is destroyed, and at that time it does not rise again — this is what is written, "How have you fallen from heaven, Helel ben Shachar" (Isaiah 14:12), "the crown of our head has fallen" (Lamentations 5:16) — these being the supernal Heh and the lower Heh, [and] Vav, the middle pillar, bearing them both — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:73: Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, in the Midrash Va'eleh HaDevarim Rabbah (1:10), said, of blessed memory: Rabbi Reuven said, and what is the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He? "Emet" (truth). And why "emet"? "Emet" has three letters — Aleph, the first of the letters; Mem, their middle; Tav, their last — to say, "I am the first, and I am the last, and besides Me there is no god" (Isaiah 44:6) — so far his words. These are the words of the Tikkunim as explained, except that it adds the matter of saying "I am the first." It is possible that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, intended these words according to the plain sense, to teach us that whoever speaks truth will find nothing added or subtracted from his words, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "I am the first and I am the last" — for what exists in His reality as the first is, in itself, also the last, and there is nothing added or subtracted for us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:74: According to the mystical sense, in the Tikkunim (119a), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains that "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no god" is said with the Name Sag (spelled with alephs), which is Yod-Kei Vav-Kei, which has three Yods, and concerning the three Yods it is said "I am the first and I am the last." In these words: and that which said "na'aseh" (let us make) is Yod-Kei Vav-Kei — "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no god" — three Yods testify concerning it that there is nothing above it. This is the very matter explained — that what is Yod at the beginning is itself Yod at the end, and the first Heh does not change from the last Heh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:75: When you examine carefully what is said in the Tikkunim in the passage we quoted, regarding the Name Yod-Kei Vav-Kei, which is the "tenth part" of truth, we understand the reason the Torah is called "the Torah of truth" — because it is attached to His great Name mentioned, this being what is explained in the Zohar several times (Parashat Yitro 90b), that the Torah is entirely the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. For this reason too the Torah is called "the Tree of Life," for truth is the mystery of the Tree of Life — "You will give truth to Jacob" (Micah 7:20) — and the Torah is called truth, as it is said, "and Your Torah is truth" (Psalms 119:142). And so "truth" is alluded to in the Name Sag in the mystery of "I am the first," and these two Names are explained in the Tikkunim as: this is the neshamah, and this is the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:76: By this we understand the reason one who speaks truth lives long, as is explained in Sanhedrin (97a) regarding that country called "the city of truth," where none of them died before his time — explained there to mean that they never varied in their speech; and once a certain sage, Rav Taviomi by name, lodged with them, and because he varied in his speech regarding a light matter, as explained there in the Gemara, he buried two of his sons, and they expelled him from among them. The reason for length of days is that the Name Mah (Mem-Heh) is the watering of the tree, in its arms and branches, as is explained in the Tikkunim (17a), in the words of Elijah; and likewise the Name Sag they call, in the Tikkunim, an explanation of neshamah — and the intent in these Names is the Cause of Causes clothed within them, as explained in the Tikkunim; it follows that one who holds fast to the supernal life, which is the life of the attributes, deserves to have his days lengthened.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:77: Also regarding the greatness of truth, the prophet explains to us in saying, "but the Lord God is truth, He is the living God" (Jeremiah 10:10). Now these two Names total, numerically, Yavak (112), equal to the count of the three Names Ehyeh, YHVH, Adonai, which are "I am the first"; it follows that one who speaks truth attaches himself to His Name, blessed be He, YHVH Elohim, which is a complete Name, as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel 213a, Idra Naso 138b), and one who attaches himself to Him attaches himself to life, as it says, "He is the living God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:78: Just as the reward is great for one who speaks truth, so the punishment is great for one who speaks falsehood, as explained in the passage from the Tikkunim, that this caused the destruction of the First and Second Temples. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain in tractate Shabbat (119b): Jerusalem was destroyed only because faithful men ceased from it, as it is said, "run to and fro..." (Jeremiah 5:1).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:79: Whoever fulfills the Torah and its commandments sustains the world, whose pillar is truth, as they say (Avot 1:17), "the world stands on three things: on judgment, on truth, and on peace." Truth is the pillar that encompasses everything, and when Israel does not occupy itself with Torah and does not fulfill it, it is written, "and it cast truth to the ground" (Daniel 8:12), as explained in the Tikkunim, and then Samael, called falsehood, rules — this is "and truth is lacking." The reason for all this is that just as the body cannot exist without a soul, so is the soul of all existing things, and the pillar that sustains them is truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:80: Included in speaking truth is that one should not speak one thing with his mouth and another in his heart, but that he be the same inside as outside — and the verse is precise about this: "the remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies, neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth" (Zephaniah 3:13). The mystery of this matter is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas 230a), in these words: and therefore the masters of the Mishnah established, "not the study is the essential thing but the deed," because the Holy One, blessed be He, is concealed in the secrets of the Torah — how is He recognized? Through the commandments, which are His Shechinah, His image. In the manner He is humble, His Shechinah is humility; He is pious, and she is pious; He is mighty, and she is mighty over all the nations of the world; He is truth, and she is faithfulness; He is a prophet, and she is prophetess; He is righteous, and she is righteous; He is King, and she is Queen; He is wise, and she is wisdom; He is understanding, and she is understanding — His crown is Keter and her crown is the crown of Tiferet. And therefore the Rabbis established: whoever is not the same inside as outside should not enter the study hall — in the image of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is "the outside," and His Shechinah is "the outside" [i.e., the visible manifestation] — He is the inside within, and she is the outside, and she does not change from what is within, to make known that she is His Atzilut, and there is no separation there at all — "within and without shall you overlay it." And because He, YHVH, is concealed within, He is called, in His Shechinah, only Adonai; and therefore the Rabbis said, "not as I am written am I called" — in this world I am written YHVH and called Adonai, but in the World to Come I am written YHVH and called YHVH, so that mercy be from every side. Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, appointed the ministering angels [to guard] that whoever is not the same inside as outside should not enter this Sanctuary, [checking] all the inner and outer limbs; and therefore the verse says, "You shall be whole with the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 18:13) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:81: This passage makes clear the greatness of one who is the same inside as outside in all his matters, and included in this is the attribute of truth — for He is truth and she is faithfulness. It follows, God forbid, that whoever does not speak truth, having deceit on his tongue, is not the same inside as outside, and he cuts the plantings, separating in the mystery of Atzilut, between the mystery of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah — as it says, "you are children to the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 14:1). For this reason the prophet said, "the remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies." Further, regarding the punishment of one who is not the same inside as outside, they elaborate in Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas 235b) and further in the Tikkunim (128b) — see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:82: Also included in truth is fulfilling the words of Torah in deed — for if one learns and does not perform, he is not included in truth. This is explained at the beginning of the passage of Ra'aya Meheimna, which says, "not the study is the essential thing but the deed, because the Holy One, blessed be He, is concealed in the secrets of the Torah — how is He recognized? Through the commandments, which are His Shechinah." Further on: He is "the inside" and she is "the outside," and she does not change from what is within, to make known that she is His Atzilut. It follows that one who expounds but does not fulfill causes separation, and shows, God forbid, that what is outside in deed does not match what is within in the speech of Torah. Therefore the deed is the essential thing, indicating the unification.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:83: And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach Lecha 163b) that truth comprises both male and female, in these words: "and Jacob was a plain (tam) man" (Genesis 25:27) — the husband of that "tam," and who is she? Aleph, the mystery of Vav-Vav. And when male and female are combined together, then it takes all these letters, Aleph-Tav-Mem, and this is Emet — "You will give truth to Jacob" — every male and female together, the completeness of everything — so far his words. It follows that whoever wishes to fulfill the quality of truth must fulfill in deed what he occupies himself with in Torah, so as to be included in Aleph-Tav-Mem, which are male and female; and this is the mystery of "and YHVH Elohim is emet" (Jeremiah 10:10), where the two Names together are the mystery of "emet."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:84: Also included in the fulfillment of truth is that one strive to be steadfast in his service like a peg that does not waver, as it is written, "and I will fasten him as a peg in a sure place" (Isaiah 22:23), and "truth" and "faithfulness" are the same matter, as explained in the passage: "He is truth and she is faithfulness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:85: Now, truth is the opposite of falsehood, for one who promises and does not do is called a liar (kazav) because he has ceased (pasak) his promise and his word — and every term of "kazav" is derived from the language of the verse, as it is written, "and like a spring of water whose waters do not fail (yechazevu)" (Isaiah 58:11). Now, the attribute of truth never ceases its mercy from the world, for it is "a river that goes out from Eden to water the garden" (Genesis 2:10), and it says "goes out," not "went out," for it always goes out; therefore Rashbi called it "a river that flows and goes out and its waters never cease" — see in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim 123b). The essential aspect of the attribute of truth depends on the Ancient One, as explained in the Idra (Parashat Naso 140b), that from there mercy never ceases — for were it conceivable, God forbid, that that flow should fail even for a moment, the world would be nullified. Likewise, a person's limbs are found at their functions — the tongue to speak, the ear to hear, the feet to walk, and the other senses — and were it conceivable that the limbs would fail to carry out their commands, the person would be nullified. Therefore the world stands on truth, and if some sense of theirs is nullified at times, it is because of the person's own cause and his deceiving in his service to the Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:86: Therefore it is fitting for a person to be steadfast in his service so that it never fails, for if he ceases, he has ceased the attribute of truth, and is in the kelipah called falsehood. It seems close to me to say that this is the attribute of deceitfulness — for what difference is there whether he deceives people or deceives the Holy One, blessed be He? And it is more fitting that one who deceives the Holy One, blessed be He, be punished than one who deceives people, as it is written, "will you mock Him as one mocks a man?" (Job 13:9).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:87: I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, that in the mouth there are thirty-two teeth, corresponding to the thirty-two [mentions of] "Elohim" in the account of Creation, which are the thirty-two paths of Chochmah; and the account of Creation is sealed with the attribute of truth (emet) at its beginning and its end — at its beginning, "Bereshit bara Elohim et" the heavens, and at its end, "bara Elohim la'asot" — to teach you that whoever lies denies the account of Creation and the thirty-two paths within it, sealed with the attribute of truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:88: This is why we find that "emet" [as an acrostic of the first and last letters of consecutive words] is mentioned six times in the account of Creation, corresponding to the six extremities sealed with the Name Yud-Heh-Vav, as is explained in Sefer Yetzirah (1:12); and these are: "Bereshit bara Elohim et," "vayar Elohim et" the light, "vayivra Elohim et" the sea monsters, "vayivra Elohim et" man, "vayar Elohim et" that which He had made, "bara Elohim la'asot" — so Rabbi Yaakov wrote in his commentary on the homiletical expositions he made on the Torah. It follows that whoever lies uproots himself from the six extremities sealed with the attribute of truth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:89: Whoever wishes not to have falsehood in his speech and dealings — if he is obligated to repay by a certain time, he should extend the time at the outset so as not to end up a liar. I have heard that this is what is meant by, "a true lip (sefat emet) shall be established forever, but a lying tongue is but for a moment" (Proverbs 12:19) — meaning, whoever is "a true lip shall be established forever" is precise, in that he extends the time greatly so that, through the passage of time, he can complete his word. But whoever says "this instant," "now," "tomorrow" — this is a lying tongue, the intent being that shortening the time is a lying tongue, since it is possible that his request will not materialize in that time and he will be found a liar. I say it is possible that for this reason the word "emet" comes alluded at the end of words rather than the beginning of words, to indicate the lengthening of time.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:90: Likewise, whoever wishes to fulfill the attribute of truth should not accustom his tongue to speaking falsehood even in matters of jest, because of "they have taught their tongue to speak lies" (Jeremiah 9:4), as we learn in Yevamot (63a) regarding Rav's wife troubling him, and so on. And not only this, but whoever fears Heaven must fulfill with his mouth what he agreed in his heart to fulfill, "and speaks truth in his heart" (Psalms 15:2), as Rav Safra fulfilled this matter, as is explained in Makkot (24a) and Bava Batra (88a) — see there.
